Subject: Dedicated capacity: GPU reservation plan & validation run

Hi Sara / Akash —

Great conversation earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can line up a dedicated validation run without surprises. I captured the points we discussed and the questions that came up on the call. Please flag anything I missed.

Key SLOs you shared (recap):
- First-byte / streaming latency: P95 first-byte <= 300 ms (SSE streaming mode)
- End-to-end P95 for short responses (<= 64 tokens): <= 350 ms
- Long-form streaming up to ~512 tokens: steady-state token throughput such that 1st-token <= 300 ms and average per-token generation <= 20 ms
- Concurrency target: 50 concurrent streaming connections (steady), with bursts up to 200 concurrent for 90s
- Sustained throughput: ~60 requests/sec (avg), peak 180 rps (2–3 minute bursts)

Traffic profile & model:
- Model: Zennify uses a 34B decoder-only model variant (fp16 / q4_0 candidate) for main workload
- Average request size: ~280 prompt tokens + ~256 generation tokens (~536 total)
- Typical session pattern: streaming first-token within 1s, then steady stream for remainder

Dedicated sizing / GPU considerations (what we recommend testing):
- A100 80GB: good baseline for FP16 34B with modest batchability; cheaper reservation footprint but may need tighter quantization (q4) for memory headroom
- H100 80GB: best headroom for larger kv cache + aggressive batching; expected lower p95 tail latency at higher concurrency but higher cost
- L40s / L4 class (if available): better price/perf on smaller prompt sizes but likely not enough headroom for sustained streaming at your token counts

Proposed validation run (what Redwood will provide):
1) Two parallel reserved configurations in our staging Dedicated cluster:
   - Config A: 2x A100 nodes (baseline)
   - Config B: 2x H100 nodes (high-headroom)
2) Run your sample workload (we'll use the sample prompts you mentioned) with the same SSE streaming client so first-byte numbers are comparable
3) Measure: first-byte P50/P95, per-token generation latency distribution, token/sec throughput, GPU utilization, and cost-per-1M-tokens estimate

What we need from you to schedule the run:
- A stable set of ~500 representative prompts (you mentioned you can share these)
- Model weights (or a container image / HF reference) and any special runtime flags you require
- Desired validation window (we proposed Mon 2026-06-15 for a four-hour window)
- Any compliance/credential requirements for running your model in our staging environment

Attachments: I attached a short workbook (Redwood-dedicated-sizing-v2.xlsx) outlining the measurement matrix and expected outputs. Also included a short GPU benchmark summary.

Next steps:
- Sara / Akash: confirm Monday (6/15) or suggest another window and upload the sample prompts + model artifact link
- We'll provision the two dedicated configs in staging and share an endpoint + test credentials by Friday EOD if 6/15 is confirmed

Thanks — looking forward to validating numbers for you.

Best,
Priyom Das

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: GPU reservation plan & validation run

Thanks Priyom — this matches our notes. A few clarifications and constraints from our infra team:

1) Streaming SLA: our product needs P95 first-byte <= 300ms under steady concurrency (50). If the first-token is > 300ms we see a degraded UX.
2) Request shape: the average total tokens per request will be closer to 520–560 (your 536 estimate is good). That makes KV cache pressure important for long sessions.
3) Burst behavior: We often see short QPS spikes when a campaign triggers: 150–220 concurrent streams for ~60–120s. We want to ensure graceful degradation vs outright failure.

We can share the prompt set and a sanitized model container. Attaching the sample prompts (zennify-sample-prompts.json). Also linking our test harness: https://gitlab.zennify.ai/test-harness (internal).

Two asks from our side before the run:
- Can Redwood run the test in SSE streaming mode (server-sent events) rather than chunked polling? We need first-byte comparability.
- On the GPU comparison: we'd prefer to see the same model on A100 (q4) vs H100 (fp16) as a like-for-like comparison — if you can do one config with quantized weights and one with fp16 that would be ideal.

If Monday 6/15 works, we can hand over the artifacts by EOD Thursday (6/11).

—Sara
Sara Chen
Head of Platform Engineering, Zennify.ai
